primitives.name: Source Health Monitor
primitives.verbatim_quote: Static records stay available when an official page is blocked, while the source-health snapshot reports `ok`, `markers_missing`, `blocked`, `auth_required`, or `error`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'status': 'dimensionless categorical variable {ok, markers_missing, blocked, auth_required, error}', 't': 'time in seconds'}
primitives.assumptions: Source availability is binary in time; static records persist despite transient blockage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When `status == blocked` or `status == error`, static records remain valid.

layer2.mapping: GSI's probabilistic source validation mirrors GSE's state machine for feed generation.

primitives.name: Feed Update Automaton
primitives.verbatim_quote: It generates a normalized JSON Feed, RSS feed, Markdown view, and a source-health snapshot: ```bash python scripts/update_sports_analytics_opportunities.py ``` The daily `update-sports-analytics-opportunities.yml` workflow runs focused tests before polling and commits only generated feed files.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F': 'feed type {JSON, RSS, Markdown}', 'S': 'source-health snapshot', 't': 'time in seconds'}
primitives.assumptions: Automated workflows generate feeds only upon data or health change.
primitives.breakdown_regime: No commit occurs unless opportunity data or source health changes.

layer2.mapping: GSE's feed generation kernel maps to GSI's conditional update logic.
layer2.telemetry: Commit frequency reflects data volatility and system responsiveness.

primitives.name: Opportunity Indexer
primitives.verbatim_quote: `mit-ssac-conference-pages` automatically indexes official 2012-2026 conference pages and currently resolves 165 public research paper/poster PDFs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'public research paper or poster', 'T': 'time range [2012, 2026]', 'N': 'number of resolved documents (165)'}
primitives.assumptions: Indexing is exhaustive over specified temporal scope and document types.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Indexing fails if PDFs are inaccessible or metadata is malformed.

layer2.mapping: GSI's opportunity scoring aligns with GSE's structured document retrieval.
layer2.telemetry: Resolved PDF count and metadata completeness.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism operates as a dual-layered system: a feed update automaton polls and conditionally commits based on data or health changes, while a source health monitor ensures persistent access to static records during outages. The opportunity indexer builds upon this by mapping temporal scopes to document collections, enabling structured discovery. These primitives form a closed-loop system where each component validates and enriches the next, maintaining data integrity across transient failures. The automaton's timestamp-only checks prevent unnecessary commits, ensuring minimal overhead. The indexer's reliance on official pages and public CDNs enforces ethical sourcing, while the health monitor provides a fail-safe for unavailable sources. This architecture supports both real-time and archival data streams, with Bayesian inference in GSI enabling adaptive response to changing source reliability.
